hypothesis: A one-way SSE2 scan over complete 32-byte ASCII blocks, followed by the strict scalar decoder from the first non-ASCII block boundary, may balance the measured 16-byte and 64-byte prefix variants. This tests an intermediate block size on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload; it does not assume that input has useful ASCII spans or claim a speedup.
notes: This is a 32-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid, distinct from repeated SIMD rescans and from T1 whole-buffer validation. Each complete skipped block is all ASCII; if a block contains any high bit, scalar decoding resumes at its known boundary and validates that byte rather than assuming it is a lead. Loads and vector tails are bounded by n. No measurements were run for this candidate; the controller should evaluate it on the official workload and correctness suite.
transformations: Replace the parent's repeated 64-byte scan inside the decoder loop with a one-way scan of complete 32-byte blocks at the known initial code-point boundary.
Skip a block only when both bounded 16-byte SSE2 loads contain no high-bit bytes; on the first block with a high bit, retain its start index for strict scalar validation of the suffix.
Retain scalar tail handling, UTF-8 validity rules, run ABI, output, and thread budget.
